correctness.rationale: The object is the ordinary transpose quotient of the complete 5×5 chessboard complex. On barycentric flags, ranks ensure that if two points in one closed simplex are identified then the action fixes their supporting vertices pointwise. Different deletions have different rank sets, hence no repeated facet in one cell. The independent bounded replay gives the full and fixed flag counts, quotient cell vector (843,8340,22110,21900,7260) and integral d²=0. In descending upper dimensions it reproduces (7260,9156,2919,173) genuine free-face pairs. In Step 2 the intended condition is absence of a higher surviving coface of the proposed free face, not absence of every higher-dimensional cell globally. Indeed, any surviving higher coface would contain at least two distinct d-faces through the proposed (d−1)-face, distinguished by their ranks. The unique surviving d-coface suffices. Integral Schur complements at unit entries split off contractible generator pairs; d²=0 justifies the corresponding deletion in adjacent degrees. The replay leaves chain ranks (1,0,0,28,0) and differential zero. The quoted connectivity bound gives simple connectivity upstairs. One can see the required special case of the orbit-space fundamental-group argument directly: based edge loops in the quotient flag complex lift successively edge by edge, choosing a translate at each lift vertex; the base diagonal vertex has a singleton orbit, so each lift is a closed loop based there. Such a loop contracts upstairs, and projecting the contraction shows simple connectivity downstairs. Hurewicz and homological Whitehead now prove the integral wedge conclusion, not just the homology calculation.
residual_risks: The full Armstrong paper was not accessible through the attempted OA route; the fixed-basepoint argument above provides an independent justification in this case.
No result for other board sizes or symmetry subgroups follows. Algebraic unit pivots alone do not prove a homotopy equivalence.

value.rationale: The complete 5×5 chessboard is a canonical small chessboard complex with known integral 3-torsion, and transposition is a natural symmetry interchanging its shores. Earlier work isolated the same orbit space and the 3-local classification but left the possible 2-primary effect of quotienting by an involution open. The exact integral answer resolves this identified gap and establishes the full homotopy type rather than reproducing a known local count.
residual_risks: The value is a complete classification of this specific canonical quotient, not a general collapse theorem for all boards.
